hookLine: Three o'clock on a Tuesday afternoon, on the mountain side of a town on Maui, an engine crew

ACT_1.quote: Hawaii has the largest single integrated Outdoor Siren Warning System for Public Safety in the world.
ACT_1.attribution: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency, its own published description

ACT_1.secondary: tested monthly with the emergency broadcast system

ACT_1.primary: On the state's own published list
ACT_1.secondary: wildfires, before any of this happened

ACT_1.quote: Tune into local Radio/TV/Cable stations for emergency information and instructions by official authorities.
ACT_1.attribution: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency, what to do when you hear a siren

ACT_1.secondary: the weather itself can outrun suppression
the first forecast naming the risk
severe fire weather possible early the following week

ACT_1.quote: The forecaster recognized that this much notice of such a warning was rare.
ACT_1.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report, April 2024

ACT_1.label: Miles an hour. The gusts the National Weather Service forecast for 8 August. A forecast, not a measurement

ACT_1.quote: There is little perceptible difference between Hawaii Red Flag criteria and a typical summer day.
Based on data collected at the Honolulu airport, which is on Oahu (not Maui).
ACT_1.attribution: Finding 8, on where the fire weather forecasts came from

ACT_2.quote: At 6:34 a.m., the fire originated off Lahainaluna Road in the unmaintained vegetation near utility pole 25 as a result of molten metallic material (sparks) ejected from the re-energization of broken power lines above.
ACT_2.attribution: County of Maui Department of Fire and Public Safety with ATF, 3 October 2024

ACT_2.secondary: Accidental - not incendiary, not natural, not undetermined

ACT_2.quote: Limited evacuation from south to north.
ACT_2.attribution: Maui Police Department traffic control log, 05:40, 8 August 2023

ACT_2.quote: No flames, no smoke, or perceptibly combusting material were observed for several hours.
ACT_2.attribution: County of Maui, on the morning fire

ACT_2.quote: High winds crippled the communications infrastructure, destroying cellular phone communication within the Lahaina region in the late morning of August 8, 2023.
ACT_2.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_2.quote: With no cellular communication, residents and tourists were not able to receive emergency alerts.
ACT_2.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_3.quote: Embers from the morning phase of the fire remained undetected and were rekindled by a severe wind event at approximately 2:52 p.m.
ACT_3.attribution: County of Maui Department of Fire and Public Safety, 3 October 2024

ACT_3.quote: Our firefighters went above and beyond their due diligence to be as confident as they could be that the fire was completely extinguished before they left the scene.
ACT_3.attribution: Assistant Chief, County of Maui, 3 October 2024

ACT_3.quote: Under the severe weather conditions on August 8, 2023, this level of mopup appears to have been insufficient.

ACT_3.label: Feet long, by twenty wide. The fire as Engine 11 reported it at 15:00

ACT_3.quote: There is one house on Lahainaluna that is fully going now. We need to stop it where you are.
Evacuate your family and pets now, do not delay. Shelter is open at Lahaina Civic Center.
ACT_3.attribution: Maui Emergency Management Agency, Wireless Emergency Alert, 16:16, 8 August 2023

ACT_3.primary: The shelter named in that message

ACT_4.label: Lives, at least. The County of Maui's figure, stated 3 October 2024

ACT_4.quote: Overwhelmed the town's limited evacuation routes, some of which were blocked by downed utility poles and electrical lines.
ACT_4.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_4.quote: Severe congestion due to parked cars along neighborhood streets hindered evacuation and response efforts.

ACT_4.secondary: trapped behind one locked gate, by the officer's own count

ACT_4.quote: Emergency responders did not have ready capability to unlock emergency gates at various locations, including schools, to facilitate evacuations.
Remove barriers from potential escape exits, such as chain link fences, gates, and boulders.
ACT_4.attribution: Finding 76's recommendation, on what police vehicles should carry

ACT_4.quote: Both systems had uninterrupted electrical power during the August 2023 fires and produced water at capacity for the duration of the fire.
Household plumbing inside of the buildings failed, allowing unrestricted flow of water.
ACT_4.attribution: Finding 24, on why the pressure fell

ACT_4.quote: There was no water coming from fire hydrants in some parts of Lahaina.
ACT_4.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_4.quote: Hawaiian Electric did not have a Public Safety Power Shut-Off program in place at the time of the fire.
Creating a receptive fuel source for arcing electrical wires.
ACT_4.attribution: Finding 29, on vegetation at the base of utility poles

ACT_4.quote: There appears to be a statewide culture of dismissing and/or under-recognizing wildfire risk. This cannot be overstated.

ACT_5.quote: I am committed to an independent, unbiased, and transparent investigation into the government actions during the fires.
ACT_5.attribution: Anne E. Lopez, Attorney General of Hawaii

ACT_5.label: Gigabytes of body-camera footage, dispatch audio, vehicle location data, interviews and documents

ACT_5.quote: Only one (1) siren from the All-Hazard Outdoor Warning Siren System was operable within the burn perimeter of the Lahaina area on August 8, 2023.
The All-Hazard Outdoor Warning Siren System had not been utilized for warning of WUI fires prior to August 8, 2023.

ACT_5.secondary: MEMA has implemented a process for activating sirens for wildfires

ACT_5.attribution: The administrator of the Maui Emergency Management Agency, asked whether he regretted not activating the sirens, 16 August 2023

ACT_5.secondary: he resigned, citing health reasons. He has not been charged with any offence

ACT_5.quote: Many residents did NOT receive a text notification from the county regarding the high winds and high fire danger.
Many refused because there did not appear to be official notification that danger was imminent.
The only missing EOC sign-in sheet is the one for MEMA personnel for August 8, 2023.
ACT_5.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_5.quote: Because of missing data, it is difficult to make a complete and accurate accounting of activities within the EOC.
ACT_5.attribution: FSRI, Lahaina Fire Comprehensive Timeline Report

ACT_5.secondary: no payment has been made; an appeal over fees is pending

ENDING.secondary: says that sounding the siren would have changed the outcome
when you hear a siren that is not a test, turn on the radio
